request.spec:
The sheet has a fiscal year start month (settings, 1 to 12, 1 unless set, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>; anything else is refused). A fiscal year is
named FY<yyyy> by the calendar year its first day falls in; show on each period the fiscal year its
from-date falls in. A year entry and a button generate that fiscal year's twelve monthly periods
exactly as the period generator does; show how many were made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a fiscal year start month (settings, 1 to 12, 1 unless set, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>; anything else is refused). A fiscal year is
named FY<yyyy> by the calendar year its first day falls in; show on each period the fiscal year its
from-date falls in. A year entry and a button generate that fiscal year's twelve monthly periods
exactly as the period generator does; show how many were made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the fiscal year start month, the fiscal year shown on each period, and a button that generates a fiscal year's periods. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**The setting.** `fiscal-start-month` is a new setting that isn't dated and is 1 unless set. The server only accepts whole numbers from 1 to 12. It stores "04" as `4`, and refuses anything else, including a blank, with `settings-error`. A save writes the usual `SETTING_CHANGED … key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>` line to the audit file. The settings form has a new field for it, with the value in force shown beside it.

**FY on each period.** A new `period-fy` column shows `FY<yyyy>` for each period's from-date. The year counts back by one when the from-date's month is before the start month. It's worked out on the screen from the current setting, so it updates as soon as the setting changes.

**Generate a fiscal year.** A new year entry and button (`period-generate-fy-year`, `period-generate-fy`) call a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/periods/generate-fy`. It turns the year into twelve months starting at the start month and hands them to the existing period generator. So a month whose name already exists or that overlaps another period is skipped, the same way as in the range generator, and each period made is audited the same way. A year that isn't four digits is refused.

The year button and the date-range button share one "made" count and one error message, because the test reads both through the same `period-generated` and `period-generate-error` elements. That shared error message now mentions the fiscal year as well as the dates.

The new server files are `ValidateGenerateFiscalYear.java` and `GenerateFiscalYearRequest.java`, plus the `generate-fy.POST.yml` route. The setting itself is added to `Settings`, `ValidateSetting` and `SettingsResponse`.
